steps: This video shows iterative refinement: diagnose, revise, verify, decide. Maya asks Claude for a quarterly client summary, and draft one comes back too long, in the wrong tone, and missing a key metric.
She rewords the request eight times, but versions six, seven and eight all bury the bottom line. The same flaw keeps repeating, and each reword gives diminishing returns.
A colleague asks: did you tell Claude what was wrong, and what you needed? Maya realises she never said. She was just guessing at new wording.
First, diagnose. Maya checks version eight against her own criteria and names exactly three flaws: it runs three pages, uses contractions, and has no churn figure.
Next, revise. One targeted follow-up names each fix: one page, no contractions, add churn. Claude returns version nine, formal, one page, with churn included.
Now verify. Maya checks version nine against the same three flaws. All three are fixed, and nothing else broke along the way.

Finally, decide. Maya accepts version nine. Had it failed, she would iterate again or change approach. Naming the exact flaws beats rewording blindly. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
